evidence.observation: A task created in one CLI process is readable with a stable id and created_at in later, separate CLI processes. The public help text states each board is a durable SQLite-backed queue with its own DB, and boards create discloses the per-board DB path. Durability beyond SQLite's documented guarantees is not claimed.
create accepts --idempotency-key and echoes the persisted task.

Re-submitting the same key returns the original task (t_6253023d) and does not create a duplicate; the board still held exactly one task. There is no standalone query-by-key command: the dedup create is the lookup. Dedup holds only while the existing task is non-archived; after archiving, the same key created a new task (observed t_c3385bd7), and a done-but-not-archived task still held its key (observed t_d191d897).
The external reference is the public task id (t_XXXXXXXX). show returns the full record; list returns the task array with status filters and sort orders.

--mutex-key serializes a task with other running tasks using the same explicit board-local key. Not exercised at runtime because observing contention requires dispatching real workers; adapter must treat board-local key scope as the verified contract boundary.

Public status enum: archived, blocked, done, ready, review, running, scheduled, todo, triage. Observed transitions on probe tasks: ready -> blocked -> ready -> done (completed_at set), ready -> archived.

For a submitted, not-yet-running task, block pauses dispatch and archive removes it from the active queue (status archived) and frees its idempotency key. Cancelling an already-running worker was not exercised and would require worker dispatch.

show exposes result and completed_at on the task record; completed_at was set by the public complete operation. The worker-side submit-result flow exists in public help but was not exercised because it requires an owned running worker.

notes: Compatibility decision: supported. All capabilities required by the durable Kanban contract are present through the public CLI; no reduced guarantee is needed for v0.19.1.

Supported Hermes version range: exactly 0.19.1 as verified on 2026-08-19. The adapter may treat >=0.19.1 <0.20.0 as the candidate range only after re-running this probe against each new version; any other version must fail route validation per HER-002/HER-005.

Version discovery is human text only: `hermes --version` prints 'Hermes Agent v0.19.1 (2026.7.30)' with no JSON mode; `hermes kanban` JSON responses do not include a version field. The adapter must gate versions by invoking `hermes --version` and matching the documented first-line format, or by configuration.

Idempotency keys are not unique forever: dedup applies only while a non-archived task holds the key. JJUKKUMI must persist the returned external task id immediately after acceptance and must not rely on key-based lookup after archival.
--assignee is not validated at create time: an unknown profile name is accepted. Validate profiles first via `hermes kanban assignees --json` (on_disk flag) or `hermes profile list`.

Runtime and retry hints: --max-runtime (seconds or durations; the dispatcher SIGTERMs then SIGKILLs and re-queues on overrun) and --max-retries (consecutive-failure circuit breaker, default 2) are per-task public fields. max-runtime acts as an enforced cap; max-retries bounds automatic retries.
Workspace binding: --workspace accepts scratch | worktree | worktree:<path> | dir:<path>; the created task echoes workspace_kind and workspace_path.
Skill selection: --skill is repeatable and echoed as the skills array; the kanban lifecycle skill is injected automatically.

Error model: unknown task and unknown board print a human message on stderr and exit 1 with a recovery hint; unrecognized arguments exit 2 (argparse); success with --json emits machine-readable JSON on stdout.
No public request-size limit is documented; maximum_request_bytes is therefore null and the adapter must enforce its own bounded manifest policy.

Webhook capabilities were inspected separately without implementation: `hermes webhook subscribe|list|remove|test` manages inbound event-driven agent activation subscriptions with an HMAC secret, event filters, optional script filter, and delivery targets; in this installation the webhook receiving platform is not enabled and `hermes webhook list` prints setup guidance. Outbound delivery adaptation remains E6-T1 scope.

All probes ran against the disposable board jjukkumi-e0t4-probe, which was hard-deleted after evidence capture; the user's active board selection was never changed and only public CLI commands were used. The per-board kanban.db path was disclosed by public CLI output but never opened or read directly.
Task ids observed in fixtures (t_6253023d, t_d191d897, t_c3385bd7) belonged to the deleted probe board and no longer exist.

E6-T1 added the outbound hermes-webhook sink adapter from the E0-T4 public interface report's s9 evidence (hermes-public-interface-report.md, 'Webhook Capabilities (Inspected Only, Not Implemented)'): the declared capability set is static and offline (durable_acceptance false, submit_idempotency_key true, all lookups/execution/cancellation/result_receipt false, maximum_request_bytes 262144), because the receiving platform is inbound-only and not enabled in the probed installation, so no response contract proves durable acceptance; a 2xx therefore maps to transport acceptance only and reachability is proven solely by submission.
